subject: Re: MAP & security sprint — SOC 2 / SIG / DPA / retention scope
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@clearbank.com>
To: priya_natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ClearBank Procurement <procurement@clearbank.com>
Date: 2026-10-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff — high level asks on security gates

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — ClearBank is excited about the latency profile and model routing features. Procurement asked me to get a short mutual action plan (MAP) in writing so we can internalize timelines for SOC 2 evidence, SIG/CAIQ answers, the DPA redline, and data residency/retention commitments.

Top asks from our side:
- SOC 2: which controls are in-scope for the hosted API vs. private deployment? We need a short controls map we can show InfoSec.
- SIG/CAIQ: expected turnaround for the questionnaire (partial responses are acceptable) and whether you can mark items as "informational" vs. "in-scope".
- DPA: can you share a redline cadence? Our legal needs to see a draft DPA and a plan to resolve vendor carve-outs (e.g., EU data residency).
- Retention: sample retention tiers and a proposed default (tokens/logs/embeddings). Any options for shorter retention windows during the evaluation?

Can you propose a one- to two-week sprint plan (MAP) that aligns evidence delivery with our procurement milestone of Oct 22 signoff? We have a narrow runway and want clarity on what is needed to unblock legal and security.

If it's helpful I can loop in our InfoSec lead (they prefer short checklists rather than long documents).

Best,
Emily
Emily Zhao
Head of Integrations, ClearBank

Attachments: none

From: priya_natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@clearbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, jordan_blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-10T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — high level asks on security gates

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear asks. I put together a compact MAP and attached three artifacts to accelerate review: a one-page SOC 2 in-scope controls mapping, our partial SIG/CAIQ workbook with status flags, and a DPA redline (first pass).

High-level (proposed MAP / 8 business days):
1) Day 0 (today): share artifacts (attached) + identify one InfoSec and one Legal reviewer on your side.
2) Day 1–2: ClearBank reviews SOC 2 controls map and SIG workbook; mark unknowns.
3) Day 3: Redwood provides short writeups for any flagged SIG items and confirms deployment model differences (hosted vs private).
4) Day 4: Legal redline pass on DPA. Redwood responds same day to critical carve-outs (data residency, subprocessors).
5) Day 5–6: Evidence handoff for SOC 2 (control testing artifacts) and final SIG sweep.
6) Day 7–8: Final DPA alignment + mutual signoff window.

Notes / constraints:
- SOC 2: hosted API is covered by our Type II report for infrastructure and platform controls; certain customer-specific operational controls (e.g., account provisioning SSO flows) remain in-customer scope. I called out the split in the attached soc2-in-scope-controls.md.
- SIG/CAIQ: we'll fill high-risk items first; we can mark low-risk items as informational to speed acceptance. See sig-caiq-partial-response.xlsx where we pre-populated ~40% of questions.
- Data retention: default evaluation mode keeps short-term logs (30 days), tokens cached for 24 hours unless customer requests longer. For POCs we can enable a 7-day short retention window with an NDA addendum — propose that as an option for ClearBank.
- DPA: redline-dpa-v1.docx captures proposed carve-outs for EU residency and KMS key control options. We're open to escrow/contractual commitments for production.

I'll coordinate internal stakeholders here (Kimberly on legal escalations and Jordan on the evidence handoff). Can you confirm who on your side will be the InfoSec reviewer and the legal reviewer? If you can reply with names by EOD Monday we can hit the Oct 22 procurement milestone.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: soc2-in-scope-controls.md (text), sig-caiq-partial-response.xlsx (spreadsheet), redline-dpa-v1.docx (Word)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Fwd: MAP kickoff — internal ops & legal alignment

Priya / Jordan — forwarding Emily's request and Priya's proposed MAP. Quick internal plan from Legal/Trust:

Action items for our side:
- Legal (Kimberly): review redline-dpa-v1.docx and highlight non-starters (I expect two possible carve-outs: EU residency SLA & KMS escrow mechanics).
- Trust (Jordan): prepare a 1–2 page evidence packet for SOC 2 controls listed as "provided by Redwood" (control IDs + sample evidence links). I can provide obfuscated sample logs and a short runbook for evidence intake.
- Solutions (Priya): confirm the short retention POC toggle and provide exact config steps for the 7-day evaluation window (we need a clear rollback plan).

Timing: We should timebox Legal review to 48 hours and Trust evidence packaging to 72 hours so Priya can respond according to the MAP cadence. If clearbank wants a shorter retention during the POC, Jordan and I will own the execution.

FYI: I flagged the DPA clause around subprocessors — we may need to propose a split-SLA approach (hosted endpoints vs. private deploy).

-K

Hi Emily — quick update after internal alignment. We can commit to the MAP timeline with the following clarifications so your team can make an internal go/no-go decision on Oct 22: 

Confirmed commitments:
- SOC 2 evidence: Redwood will deliver the control evidence packet for all platform-owned controls by Oct 15. You'll get a short index (control id -> artifact link) plus an anonymized sample for log retention.
- SIG/CAIQ: we will complete high-risk rows and mark low-risk rows as informational by Oct 13. The worksheet will include a column "status" (provided / pending / informational).
- DPA: Redwood will accept most redlines; we request a 48-hour review cycle on our responses. For EU residency we propose two paths: (A) private deployment (customer-managed VPC) or (B) contractual residency commitment with CSP region pinning and data escrow for agreed retention tiers.
- Retention: default eval mode = 30-day logs / 24-hour token cache. For the POC we enable an opt-in 7-day retention config (no embeddings persisted) — Jordan will provide the toggle and rollback instructions.

Next steps for ClearBank: please confirm InfoSec reviewer (name + email) and Legal reviewer by Mon 10/14 so we can start the 48-hour legal window. If you want, Kimberly is available for a quick call Tue morning to talk DPA carve-outs.

If that all looks good I'll create a short MAP doc with milestone checkboxes and share a HubSpot ticket so procurement can track signoffs.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
